title: runtime-economics-and-reliability-bridge

transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2025-06-05 16:00 UTC | Duration: 52m | Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Grant (Redwood SE), Sofia (Redwood CSM), Tom, Anika, Marcus, Jill

Summary (auto): quick review of May cost spike and a short canary latency regression. Discussed short-term mitigations and pilot for Dedicated.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, quick roll call?
[00:05] Tom: tom here, hi Maya, Anika and Marcus on my side too.
[00:08] Anika: yeah hi, thanks for the time.
[00:12] Maya: great, so agenda, spike in token spend in May, the 20-min latency bump on our canary, and pilots/options. Grant's got the bench data. Grant over to you.
[00:23] Grant: cool thanks. so we reproduced the latency regress on the canary route, looks like a KV cache warm-up plus an unexpected batch coalescing delay when requests hit sequence lengths above 2k. the runtime picks a different kernel path and we see P95 jump from ~220ms to ~680ms for that burst.
[00:45] Marcus: uh yeah we saw that, it correlated with their new long-form summarize endpoint, which got rolled last week, traffic was spiky.
[00:55] Anika: is that the new summarize-v2? we thought the token cost increases were mostly due to embeddings but sounds like generation is the culprit.
[01:04] Jill: from finance perspective we see a 38% month over month jump versus the forecast, need to triage asap.
[01:12] Grant: right, two contributors: longer sequence lengths (more tokens per request) and the canary hitting a kernel fallback path that increases latency and causes retry-induced duplicate tokens for some clients. also kv cache warm cold effect — we saw K V cash spelled out in some logs, transcription funny — but basically prefix caching isn't warm for new pods.
[01:34] Maya: ok so mitigation layers: quick wins are prefix caching warmup, reducing model context length for that route, or increasing dedicated capacity for hot routes. medium: tune autoscale thresholds to avoid too many scale-ups during traffic spikes. longer: Dedicated pool for those endpoints.
[01:50] Tom: can you quantify the cost delta if we moved the two highest QPS endpoints to Dedicated? we need a number.
[01:58] Maya: yes we'll send a per-route cost export, but ballpark, if you commit for reserved capacity you'd see per-token unit drop around 15-30% depending on sustained QPS and batching. we'll put exact numbers in the CSV.
[02:15] Marcus: what's the work to get VPC access? security folks asked about KMS integration and audit logs.
[02:22] Sofia: we have a checklist, SOC2/ISO artifacts, and a VPC onboarding doc. for KMS we support bring-your-own-key via our KMS connector, there are a few steps but it's standard. I'll share the checklist after the call.
[02:36] Anika: timeline: we want to avoid a big ops lift, can we run a minimal Dedicated pilot for two endpoints for two weeks? scope = /api/generate and /summarize-v2.
[02:46] Grant: technically straightforward. we'll need traffic profile and target SLOs to size. if you give us QPS and P95 targets we can map to a minimal GPU pool.
[02:57] Tom: QPS for generate is around 45 sustained with peaks to 120, summarize-v2 is 12 sustained, peaks to 40. P95 we want below 450ms ideally.
[03:09] Grant: ok that helps. note: batching helps unit cost but affects latency, for generate we can tune batching window smaller and use continuous batching to keep latency under target while retaining throughput.
[03:24] Jill: also need billing visibility daily during pilot. can we get token-level splits per route?
[03:30] Maya: yes we'll provide daily CSV for pilot.
[03:34] Marcus: can Redwood push canary config that warms prefix cache on new instances? that's critical.
[03:39] Grant: yes we have an option to pre-warm the KV cache using synthetic warmup requests; we can run that as part of deploy hooks. it's an ops job but doable.
[03:49] Anika: any other quick wins we should try before committing to Dedicated?
[03:52] Maya: reduce context length for summarize-v2 or use quantization profile the runtime suggested; those lower per-token cost but we should validate quality. Redwood Optimize can provide recommendations.
[04:03] Tom: quality matters, we can't degrade summarize outputs. can we A/B test quantized variant?
[04:07] Grant: yes canary with small % traffic then compare eval metrics, we can instrument automatic rollback if scores drop.
[04:15] Sofia: I'll capture that as part of the pilot plan and include eval prompts.
[04:20] Jill: finance wants cost runbook for spikes, e.g., automatic routing to cheaper model variant if cost breakeven hits. is that supported?
[04:28] Maya: yes smart routing lets you define policies by latency/cost. you can fallback to a smaller model variant in peak if quality tolerates it. we'll share examples.
[04:36] Marcus: security note: for Dedicated pilot we need a contract appendix for data residency and audit log export retention to S3.
[04:44] Maya: we'll loop legal and provide the appendix template and our retention SLAs.
[04:49] Tom: timeline recap? can we have the bench and cost numbers by Monday?
[04:53] Maya: yes, we'll push the cost CSV and initial sizing by 2025-06-07. Grant will kick off the 48h bench today/tomorrow and share results by 2025-06-10.
[04:59] Grant: we'll also include verbose logs and kernel path traces so you can see the fallback.
[05:05] Anika: OK thanks, action items?
[05:08] Maya: recap in email, include links: cost export, bench folder, SOC2 checklist, pilot kickoff calendar invite.
[05:14] Tom: appreciated, thanks everyone.
[05:16] Maya: thanks all, we'll follow up.

End of transcript. Notes: occasional transcription errors (K V cash for KV cache, Redwood Dedicate vs Dedicated). There was mild crosstalk during the Q&A.
